messages:
ash: Quick proposal for a canonical loadtest protocol to compare synthetic vs replay traffic and surface KV-cache interactions + kernel selection effects.
--
ash: TL;DR: run 3-phase jobs (calibration, synthetic, replay) with identical model config, seed, and batching caps; report TTFT, TPOT, p95/p99, goodput, and QPS. Include kernel attribution and KV cache hit profiles.

maria: can you spell out the "apples-to-apples" checklist? what exactly must be identical across runs?

ash: short list: model weights+quantization, sequence length distribution, max_batch_size, max_concurrent_requests, input RNG seed, request arrival timestamps (for replay), and timeout/SLO settings. also same device type and kernel selection policy.

kevin: add: same prefix caching state (warm vs cold) and same fallback routing policies. small differences there kill goodput numbers.

jon: agree. we should capture both cold-start (empty KV) and warmed KV scenarios. propose: N=2 modes per run: kv_warm=true and kv_warm=false with a standard warmup trace.

sophia: re metrics: can we clarify definitions? my note:
- TTFT = time from request ingress to first token emitted
- TPOT = time from first token to final token (post-first-token time)
- goodput = tokens generated / GPU-second (or tokens/sec while GPU busy)
- QPS = requests started / sec (includes idle gaps)
- p95/p99 computed on TTFT and TPOT separately

maria: how do we measure kernel attribution? per-token kernel mapping sounds heavy.

ash: instrument runtime to emit per-request summaries: dominant kernel (attention, matmul, fused-op) by token percentile, and percent time spent in kernel vs queuing. something like:
```
{ "req_id": "r123", "ttft_ms": 85, "tpot_ms": 320, "kernels": {"matmul": 210, "attn": 80, "other": 30}, "kv_hits": 0.65 }
```
we'll aggregate these to get kernel-level p50/p95 and percent-of-total.

kevin: for batching heuristics experiments, let's keep the request inter-arrival process constant and only toggle the heuristic: fixed-batch (size=N), adaptive-latency (target-ms=T), and continuous-batching (greedy). record batch size distribution.

jon: instrumentation checklist: trace ids, batch_id, kernel name, kernel time (ns), cpu->gpu memcpy times, kv lookup latency, batch queue wait time. also record memory footprint samples (peak KV size / GPU memory).

perf-bot: summary uploaded: run 2026-02-18T08:23Z, job=rv1-loadcomp, artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/rv1/1767773333/

sophia: example harness command to be committed to infra repo:
```
harness run --job=rv1-loadcomp \
  --mode=compare \
  --trace=prod-sample-20260201 \
  --synthetic-profile=seq-dist.json \
  --kernels=auto,optimized \
  --kvcache=on,off \
  --batching=fixed,adaptive,continuous \
  --seed=42
```

maria: when we publish results, show both QPS curves and goodput curves side-by-side. emphasize SLO compliance: fraction of requests with TTFT < X ms and TPOT < Y ms. include boxplots for kernel times.

kevin: quick question: how do we avoid overfitting heuristics to the chosen replay trace? we want broader signal.

ash: run with multiple replay traces (weekdays, peak hour, long-chat heavy) + synthetic mixtures sampled from production seq-length histogram. produce per-trace aggregated deltas.

jon: for regressions, set automatic alert rules: >5% p95 TTFT regression or >10% goodput regression vs baseline triggers a reclamation build and kernel profiler run.

sophia: i'll prep a short PR to add the per-kernel counters and batch-size histogram to the runtime telemetry.

ash: perfect. next step: owners (sophia+jon) implement counters; kevin builds comparison dashboard; maria drafts the runbook. we aim to run full-suite next Monday.

maria: :thumbsup:

jon: noted, starting on trace harness changes.

perf-bot: regression check scheduled: baseline=1765000000, compare=1767773333, notifications to #eng-runtime if threshold exceeded.
